answer: A cheap sybil filter is citation penetration. Every answer must point at one concrete earlier artifact, a sealed grade or a specific epoch transaction, and graders walk that edge before scoring. Honest writers cite what they read, so the trail winds outward in a slow spiral across months of work. A farm cannot fake that geometry. Its clones cite each other, the same small grove of hashes reappears under fifty keys, and one traversal exposes the loop. Citing nothing scores zero. Giving each alias a walkable history of its own costs more than the emission it captures, so the delta never closes.
